title: Tamil Nadu Budget 2026 LIVE updates: State Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson to present TVK government's maiden Budget
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
• August 05, 2026 08:33
    White Paper addresses adverse impact of ‘revenue collapse’ on people of Tamil Nadu

    Expressing concern over what the State government’s White Paper termed a “revenue collapse” in Tamil Nadu, the document is of the view that the trend is hurting the people of the State in three ways.

    Ahead of today’s Budget, click here to read more on what the White Paper says...

  • August 05, 2026 08:04
    Heightened expectations for Vijay-led TVK government's maiden Budget

    Amid heightened expectations, the maiden Budget of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led coalition government in Tamil Nadu headed by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay will be presented in the Legislative Assembly on Wednesday (August 5, 2026). Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson will present the State Budget for 2026-27 at 10 a.m. in the Assembly.

    The Budget assumes added significance as the TVK had made several promises on the welfare front ahead of the 2026 Assembly election and is now expected to outline its roadmap for fulfilling them. Many of the party’s poll promises require substantial financial resources for their implementation.

    Click here to read more on this...

    As the new Tamil Nadu government led by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay gears up to present its first budget on Wednesday, here is a look back at the State’s finances, with charts explaining the changes over the years, how Tamil Nadu fares compared with its peers and the challenges ahead.

title: A history of Namakkal Kavignar Maaligai that will house Tamil Nadu CM Vijay’s new office
author: T. Ramakrishnan
content_html:
The 10-storeyed Namakkal Kavignar Maaligai on the campus of Fort St. George in Chennai is in news these days as Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has decided to move to the 10th floor of the building and function from there.

At present, he works from the main block of the 17th century vestige of British rule. Compared to the heritage structure, the Maaligai is a recent building, which is about 50-years old. It houses a number of government departments, providing accommodation to many senior IAS officers and other officials. Over the years, the Maaligai has become a major power centre, as most of the departments are located there. Till the construction of this building, the Secretariat functioned from the main block due to which the government staff enormously suffered for want of space, recalls N. Ganapathy, a veteran journalist who covered the Secretariat for various newspapers between the 1960s and the 1990s.

title: Only one of four Bengaluru suburban rail corridors clears land hurdle
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
More than four years after the Bengaluru Suburban Rail Project (BSRP) received approval, only one of its four corridors has completed land acquisition, while another has acquired just 7.8 acres of the required 57 acres, according to a reply by the Union government in the Lok Sabha.

The ₹15,767-crore project has incurred an expenditure of ₹2,659 crore so far, with delays attributed mainly to pending land acquisition and transfer of State government land.

Replying to an unstarred question recently by Chickballapur MP K. Sudhakar in the Lok Sabha, Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the 148.17-km BSRP is being implemented by Rail Infrastructure Development Company (Karnataka) Limited (K-RIDE), a company in which the Karnataka government holds a 51% stake. The project is funded with 20% each by the Centre and the State government, while the remaining 60% is to be raised through debt.

Among the four corridors, Corridor-2 (Mallige), connecting Baiyyappanahalli and Chikkabanavara over 25.01 km, has made the most progress. The government said land acquisition has been completed in full, separate contracts have been awarded for station buildings, and construction is under way. Tenders have also been invited for the remaining works.

Status

For Corridor-1 (Sampige) between KSR Bengaluru city and Devanahalli (41.4 km), alignment plans have been approved, while land acquisition is under way. Shifting of signalling, telecommunication (S&T) and electrical utilities has also commenced.

A similar status was reported for Corridor-3 (Parijaata), the 35.52-km line connecting Kengeri and Whitefield. The alignment has been approved, while land acquisition and utility shifting are currently in progress.

Progress has been slowest on Corridor-4 (Kanaka), which will connect Heelalige and Rajankunte over 46.25 km. Of the 57 acres required for the corridor, only 7.8 acres have been acquired so far. However, contracts for station buildings have been awarded, and construction has begun on the land already available.

Non-acquisition of private land

The Union government said that the project has been delayed due to the non-acquisition of private land and the transfer of State government land by the Government of Karnataka. It added that regular coordination meetings are being held between K-RIDE and the Railways to resolve pending issues and expedite implementation.

While the Lok Sabha question sought revised completion timelines for the Mallige and Kanaka corridors, the government did not specify any fresh deadlines in its reply. It, however, reiterated that efforts are continuing to address land acquisition and coordination issues affecting the project’s progress.

title: Chola idols of Gajasamharamurti in Tamil Nadu depict Lord Shiva’s valour and ferocity
author: B. Kolappan
content_html:
Vazhuvur, a small town in Mayiladuthurai district, occupies a special place in both the Saivite tradition and the history of Bharatanatyam. It is one of the Ashta Veerattanams — the eight sacred shrines where Lord Shiva is believed to have manifested his valour through heroic deeds.

Vazhuvur is equally renowned as the birthplace of Vazhuvoor Ramaiah Pillai, one of the foremost Bharatanatyam gurus of the 20th century, who also choreographed dance sequences for Tamil films. The Vazhuvur bani, one of the principal schools of Bharatanatyam, traces its origins to him.
